summary: K. N. Neelakantan Elayath was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He served as an Assistant Professor at Government Arts College (1967–1969) and Sree Krishna College (1972–1984), before becoming Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calicut (1990–2003).

K. R. Norman (1925–2020) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Downing College, Cambridge, under Harold Walter Bailey. He taught at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and edited the Pali Text Society Journal (1981–1994).

K. S. Balasubramanian is a scholar of Indology and philosophy affiliated with the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute, where he served on the Editorial Committee (attested 2001) and as Director (attested 2026).

id: P:K. S. J. M. de Vreese
summary: K. S. J. M. de Vreese (1906–1992) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He completed his studies and Ph.D. under Jean Philippe Vogel at Leiden University, later teaching Pāli there (1948–1963) and serving as professor at the University of Amsterdam (1960–1981).
K. Sambasiva Sastri (1879–1946) was an Indology scholar who served as Curator at the Department of Oriental Manuscripts Publications from circa 1924 to 1935, succeeding T. Ganapati Sastri.

K. Srinivasan is an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Ramakrishna Mission Vivekananda College and held the Brahmasri Anna Subramaniam Chair at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (attested 2020–2026).

K. V. J. Koshalee specializes in Buddhist studies and archaeology. Educated at the University of Kelaniya and the Postgraduate Institute of Archaeology, she held posts at Kelaniya, the University of Ruhuna (2025), and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies (2026).
K. V. Puttappa (1904–1994) was a linguistics scholar who studied at Hardwick High School and College, Maharaja's College, Mysore (circa 1925–1929), and the University of Mysore (circa 1927–1929).

K. V. Raman (1934–2024) studied at Madras Christian College under A. J. Boyd, the University of Madras, and the Institute of Archaeology, ASI. He worked for the Archaeological Survey of India (c. 1957–1976) and was Professor at the University of Madras (1976–1995).

K. V. Ramesh (1935–2013) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Secretary of the Epigraphical Society of India, Director of Epigraphy at the Archaeological Survey of India (attested 1981–1987), and Honorary Director at Oriental Research Institute Mysore (attested 2012).
K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar (1880–1960) was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Principal of Central Hindu College and Banaras Hindu University circa 1935–1940.

K. Venkata Ramanan worked in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Sentian Wang, and earned a D.Litt. from Visva-Bharati University under Prabodh Chandra Bagchi, later teaching at Visva-Bharati.

K. de B. Codrington (1899–1986), an Indologist and archaeologist, studied at Corpus Christi College and Wadham College. He served as Professor at the University of Cincinnati, Keeper at the Victoria and Albert Museum (1935–1948), and Professor of Indian Archaeology at SOAS (1948–1966).

Kaetan Andreevich Kossovich (1815–1883) was an Indology and Iranian/Central Asian scholar who studied at Moscow State University under Aleksej Stepanovič Homjakov. He taught at Tver Gymnasium, worked at the National Library of Russia, and became Professor of Sanskrit at Saint Petersburg State University.

id: P:Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso
summary: Kah Tok Wön Trul Tsultrim Yönten Gyatso studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.

Kai Donner (1888–1935) was a scholar of linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied under Otto Donner and at the University of Cambridge, later holding a post at the University of Helsinki from circa 1924 to 1935.

Kaie Mochizuki (born 1959) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He has served as a professor of Buddhism (attested 2015) and as president (attested 2026) at Minobusan University.
Kaigen Noritake is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Kenyu Mitomo and served as an assistant professor at Rissho University (attested 2007).

Kaikyoku Watanabe (1872–1933) studied under Ernst Leumann at the University of Strasbourg. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he held professorships at Shukyo, Toyo, Kokushikan, and Taisho Universities, and was principal of Shiba Junior & Senior High School.

Kaiten Nukariya (1867–1934) studied under Ryodo Nukariya and at Keio University. A Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar, he lectured at Harvard University (circa 1913–1915) and served as the first president of Komazawa University (1925–1934).
